solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In a bit of language this writer conveys men with soft edge

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so the writer's word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the setter referring to themself gives ME
OR is the crossword abbreviation for other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
P is piano, the musical marking for soft
a hem is the finished edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A writer smuggling some gentle-edged men into a scrap of language.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists call the smallest meaningful unit of a word, like a prefix or stem, by this term.

clue.text: Plague of burrowing creatures, source of trouble

parts.note: moles are small animals that dig tunnels underground

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An infestation of burrowing animals is causing a gardener trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to pester or harass them, which is one sense of this verb.

clue.text: A horrible person, first to last, [one] not much good

definitions.text: A horrible person, first to last, [one] not much good

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is shifted round to the end

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved, unpleasant child or person
A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: only a little of the word is used, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone awful through and through is described as being of little worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, so it is both wordplay and definition; 'not much good' gives just the first letter of good.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratbag is informal British and Australian slang for a nasty, worthless person, a rotter.

clue.text: Has anger spreading round university to be manifested in rants?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed around the university's letter
the letters of the two words are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Is anger at a university likely to come out as ranting?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' rearranges HASANGER to HARANGES, and 'round' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches aimed at an audience are tirades, the plural noun matching the plural definition.

clue.text: Three times I tell army cop about his organisation

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: the letter I written three times

explanation.surface: Telling an army cop about the body he belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' shuffles IIITELLARMYCOP; 'his' refers back to the army cop in the surface, so the cop's organisation is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Military police are the force that army cops belong to, so it is their organisation.

clue.text: Economical floor covering with flower as border

indicators.note: the river's letters border the floor covering on both sides

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a rug is a small carpet on the floor

explanation.surface: A thrifty floor covering edged with a floral border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom, but in crosswords it is something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrifty who avoids waste is sparing with money, which is what both words describe.

clue.text: Religious type appears as a saint when captured by artist

indicators.note: the artist's letters hold the other pieces as captives inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A believer appears as a saint in an artist's painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Rastafarianism, the Jamaican faith, are known by this short name.

clue.text: Frenzied attempt to make money from natural mineral or plant

parts.note: gold is a precious metal found in nature
a rush is a grasslike marsh plant

explanation.surface: Trying to get rich quick from minerals or plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede of prospectors to a new goldfield, like California in 1849, is the classic hasty scramble for wealth.

clue.text: Huge area with millions traversed by girl

indicators.note: the girl's letters run across the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
and can mean with, as in bread and butter
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A girl crossing a vast area with millions of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent or large mass of land is a huge stretch of territory.

clue.text: It may involve work late in the evening

definitions.text: It may involve work late in the evening

parts.words: It may involve work late in the evening
parts.note: a literary work, a book, is taken up just before sleep, not overtime at the office

explanation.definitionFit: Reading a book in bed before going to sleep is a late-evening activity involving a written work.

clue.text: In the side subsequently, getting goal having expended energy

parts.note: later means afterwards, subsequently

indicators.note: using up the energy removes it from the word

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A side scoring a goal later on after running out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having expended' takes GO out of GOAL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything situated at the side or flank of something is described with this adjective.

clue.text: One Greek character or another gaining Latin in the course of long period

indicators.note: during a period, so the pieces sit within it

parts.note: an eon is a vast age

indicators.note: gaining means the first piece gets the next added on

parts.note: another Greek letter, the psi

explanation.surface: One Greek letter or another picks up some Latin over a long era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' points to a second Greek letter, the one that joins Latin's L inside the long period.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to short E, is a character from that script.

clue.text: Country home to the east of Cheltenham?

indicators.note: in an across clue the eastern piece is written to the right, after

parts.note: Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, England, is a spa town, an example of a spa
in means at home

explanation.surface: A country residence located east of the English town of Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Cheltenham as an example of a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian kingdom with Madrid as capital is a nation, a country.

clue.text: Great fussing aboard public vehicle on account of four-letter word

indicators.note: the jumbled letters ride inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a public transport vehicle on rails

indicators.note: fussing means fidgeting, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A great fuss on a tram over a rude four-letter word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fussing' turns GREAT into ETRAG, which goes 'aboard' TRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names any word of four letters, notably the Hebrew name of God, YHWH.

clue.text: See us impress with act out of the ordinary? We don't think everyone's equal

indicators.note: the letters are made unusual by being put in a different order

explanation.surface: An unusual act to impress us, from people who believe some are better than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Racial or other bigots who believe their group is superior reject the idea that all are equal.

clue.text: Alliances being supported by type to infiltrate spies

indicators.note: the pieces get inside the spy agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, so its spies
in a down clue, a piece on top of another is supported by it
sort means type or kind

explanation.surface: Alliances supported by a certain type of agent sent to infiltrate spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of companies or bodies joining forces for a venture are associations of partners, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Bit of film within film starts to interest cinema circle

indicators.note: the piece of film is placed inside the title of the other film

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
a clip is a short extract from a film

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A short extract from a film inside a film, arousing interest among cinema-goers.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use the term for the great circle of the sun's apparent path across the sky.

clue.text: Peg wants dram, Albert's not touching the stuff

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Peg wants a drink of whisky, but Albert is abstaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name, but it is the golfer's TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from all alcohol avoids drink, 'the stuff' in idiom.

clue.text: Applause when trapped animals can be seen rolling over? That's mean!

indicators.note: the reversed animals are caught inside the applause

parts.note: cheering is loud applause

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round so it is read backwards

parts.note: apes are animals

explanation.surface: Animals trapped and rolling over to applause: what a mean thing to do!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling over' turns the animals into SEPA; 'can be seen' is only a link. 'That's mean!' looks like an exclamation but holds the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-pinching stinginess, as though paring cheese rind thin, is the adjective for miserly behaviour.

clue.text: What could make the ruddy paper change?

definitions.text: What could make the ruddy paper change?

parts.words: What could make the ruddy paper change?
parts.note: red litmus paper turns blue when dipped in a base, not a swear-word newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A base such as soda turns red litmus test paper blue, which is the change described.

clue.text: Cooler individual disposing of drug, one getting caught

indicators.note: the single letter is caught inside the shortened word
the drug is got rid of, removed from the word

parts.note: a person is an individual
E is ecstasy, the drug
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who dumps drugs and then gets caught ends up in the cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposing of' removes E from PERSON, leaving PRSON, and 'getting caught' puts I inside it. 'Cooler' is slang for jail, not a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooler is slang for a jail cell, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Among other things provided by trendy retail — unusual article

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Among other things, fashionable shops stock an unusual item.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in English to mean amongst other matters or items.

clue.text: Maybe princess is born after a king's ascent

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
in a down clue an ascent reads the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king
nee is used before a maiden name, meaning born

explanation.surface: A princess was born after a king came to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascent' turns A R into RA, and NEE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu queen or princess holds this title, so a princess is an example.

clue.text: Some minstrel going about — one with an eye for the ladies?

definitions.text: one with an eye for the ladies?

indicators.note: about turns the letters round to be read backwards
some of the words' letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A wandering minstrel who likes looking at women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RELGO from inside minstrel going, and 'about' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who leers or stares at women has an eye for them; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Huge fear when head is bitten off by bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off the word

parts.note: panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: Gripped by fear when a bird bites someone's head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Huge' links to the giant Greek Titans, which is why the adjective means enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something colossal, like the mythical Greek giants, is enormous in scale.

clue.text: One man's keeping collection of books in office receptacles

indicators.note: the first pieces keep the books inside them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ray's, the possessive of a man's name
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: One man is keeping a library of books in his office trays.
explanation.definitionFit: Trays on office desks hold incoming letters and paperwork, so they are receptacles.

clue.text: About to go across the Channel as a visitor

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
aller is French, spoken across the English Channel, for to go

explanation.surface: About to travel over the Channel to visit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls at your house drops in for a visit, so a visitor.

clue.text: Concerned with land management, a senior lady crosses a sort of valley

indicators.note: the senior lady's letters go across, enclosing the valley

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, an older lady
a ria is a long drowned river valley

explanation.surface: Interested in farming, a grandmother walks across a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' in the clue is only a link word, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies relating to farmland and its cultivation are described by this adjective.
